title: Repository-wide date precision audit
evidence_level: Structured repository audit plus source review
summary: Every birth, death, and timeline date was parsed and inventoried. Legacy values ending in January 1 were compared with their cited source descriptions and prioritized for direct-record searches. Where no reviewed source explicitly established January 1, the original stored value remains available for provenance while the public display now shows only the supported year. Exact replacements are limited to dates directly stated by reviewed sources.
why_it_matters: The timeline no longer turns a known year into a fictional New Year's Day. Exact, year-only, approximate, and unknown values now sort consistently and display honestly.
claims_added_or_updated: Grace Reed Beverage birth: 1909-01-01 to 1909-10-31, exact
Grace Reed Beverage death: 2008-01-01 to 2008-06-07, exact
Lowell Pierson Beveridge birth: 1905-01-01 to 1905-09-19, exact
Lowell Pierson Beveridge death: 1991-01-01 to 1991-06-18, exact
Grace death timeline event: 2008-01-01 to 2008-06-07, exact
remaining_questions: Obtain original vital-record images for the unresolved year-only dates
Confirm whether any retained January 1 values are genuine exact dates before marking them exact

title: Grace Reed Beverage obituary resolves two placeholder dates
summary: The Kennebec Journal obituary states that Grace was born to Robert George Reed and Annie MacKinnon Reed on October 31, 1909 in Boston and died June 7, 2008 at her son's home in Pittsfield. It also documents her schooling, insurance-agency work, 1948 home purchase, five children, and time in Florida and North Haven.
why_it_matters: It supplies two full dates and a much richer life history while exposing a place-and-age conflict for family review rather than silently erasing the earlier narrative.
unresolved_conflicts: The existing profile and timeline associate the death with Dresden and age 99; the obituary says Pittsfield and age 98. The existing non-date wording remains preserved.

title: Lowell Pierson Beveridge: music, ministry, and scholarship
evidence_level: Tier 2 institutional archive plus Tier 3 contemporary obituary
summary: Lowell Beveridge was a Harvard-trained musicologist, organist, conductor, educator, and Episcopal priest. Columbia University documents his 1930–1952 faculty service, university-organist role, and efforts to strengthen its music collections. His obituary traces later service at Union Theological Seminary and Virginia Theological Seminary and records his death on June 18, 1991.
why_it_matters: A previously skeletal profile now has exact life dates and a documented multi-institution career.
unresolved_conflicts: The existing profile says North Haven as birthplace; published references say Boston or Dorchester. The existing place remains pending a birth record.

title: Harold H. Beverage and the directional wave antenna
evidence_level: Tier 1 patent plus Tier 2 IEEE records
summary: IEEE sources identify North Haven-born Harold Henry Beverage as a pioneer of transoceanic radio reception. His 1921 U.S. patent describes the directional receiving system later known as the Beverage antenna. IEEE's biography and oral history document his University of Maine education, GE and RCA career, professional leadership, wartime consulting, more than forty patents, and major engineering honors.
why_it_matters: This is the strongest newly documented career story in the archive, grounded in an original patent and professional institutional records.
remaining_questions: Obtain Harold's birth record to confirm the parent link
Locate reusable public-domain copies of the 1915 yearbook portrait and patent drawings before adding images

why_it_matters: Visitors can distinguish a broken source from a source that is merely indexed, redirected, account-gated, or potentially paywalled.

title: Repository-wide historical life and timeline expansion
evidence_level: Source-first review emphasizing official, institutional and contemporary records
summary: A systematic pass over the 180-profile archive targeted historical substance rather than new relationships. Strong discoveries include the Beverage family’s multigenerational Vinalhaven town-office service; Benjamin Beverage’s 1819 constitutional-convention role, surviving history manuscript and 1823 Maine House service; Nathaniel Beverage’s 1828 House service; the 1848 Pulpit Harbor bridge authorization adjoining James and Josiah Beverage land; Orris Beverage’s Colby/education record; Frank Beverage’s town-finance, auction and federal-petition activity; Harold Beverage’s early Carpathia wireless episode; and richer military, professional, missionary, maritime and community histories for twentieth-century relatives.
why_it_matters: The archive now shows what family members did and how they interacted with island, state, national and world events instead of presenting most people only as names and dates.

Find primary death evidence for the Benjamin Crabtree Beverage diphtheria tradition

title: Mercury/tannery death story remains uncorroborated
evidence_level: Research Lead — existing cemetery-derived claim, no independent contemporaneous corroboration located
summary: The inherited timeline attributes Jemima Crabtree Beverage’s 1837 death and the December 1850 deaths of James Beverage and daughter Lucy C. Beverage to mercury or mercurial exposure associated with James’s tannery. The current base entries ultimately cite a Find a Grave memorial. Targeted searches were run for the three people, North Haven/Vinalhaven, tannery/tanning, mercury/mercurial/quicksilver, hemorrhage and poisoning variants, including historical newspapers and the 1889 Vinalhaven history. No independent contemporaneous or official source establishing mercury poisoning was located in this pass.
why_it_matters: This is a memorable family story and therefore especially important to label honestly. The archive preserves the tradition but no longer presents the poisoning mechanism as if it had already been independently verified.
remaining_questions: Locate North Haven/Vinalhaven physician, coroner, church or town death records for 1837 and December 1850
Search unindexed regional newspaper microfilm around December 5–10, 1850
Identify the original source behind the Find a Grave narrative and determine whether it cites a family manuscript or primary record
Investigate what tanning chemicals James Beverage’s operation actually used before assuming mercury exposure
